## Q1
The famous 'Wood's Despatch' is often described as the \_\_\_\_\_\_ of English education in India.

## Q1 - Options
(A) Bill of Rights
(B) People's Charter
(C) Preamble
(D) Magna Carta

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2025 (6 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q38

**Wood’s Despatch** of 1854 is universally referred to as the **Magna Carta of English Education in India**.

- **Historical Background:** Formulated by Sir Charles Wood, President of the Board of Control of the English East India Company, it laid down the first comprehensive, articulated plan for the spread of education throughout India.
- **Key Recommendations:**
   
   - Establishment of universities on the model of London University at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras (established in 1857).
   - Creation of a Department of Public Instruction in each presidency/province.
   - Introduction of a grants-in-aid system to encourage private enterprise in education.
   - Emphasis on primary education in the vernacular languages and higher education in English.

## Q18
The Union Government's mandate for the Humayun Kabir Committee was to explore the possibility of:

## Q18 - Options
(A) Privatisation of public universities
(B) Setting up of new university
(C) Establishing correspondence courses
(D) Funding private universities

## Q18 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q21

The Humayun Kabir Committee (1964) was appointed by the Union Government to review the growing pressure on India's higher education system. Its specific mandate was to explore the feasibility and necessity of **establishing new universities** to meet regional demand, rather than expanding existing ones indefinitely.

The other options are incorrect because:

- Privatisation of public universities (A) was specifically **recommended against** by the committee, which emphasised affordable public access.
- Correspondence courses (C) were championed by separate initiatives; the committee's focus was on conventional new universities.
- Funding private universities (D) was outside the committee's primary scope.

## Q20
As per the recommendation of the National Education Policy (2020), Indian standards of skills will be aligned with the International Standard Classification of Occupations of:

## Q20 - Options
(A) UNDP
(B) UNESCO
(C) ILO
(D) ITU

## Q20 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q42

The National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) sets out to map Indian skill qualifications onto a globally recognisable framework. It specifies alignment with the **International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO)**, which is maintained by the **International Labour Organization (ILO)** — the UN agency responsible for labour standards.

ISCO provides a hierarchical system for classifying and organising all occupations, enabling comparison of skill levels and job families across countries. This alignment allows Indian vocational and higher-education qualifications to be benchmarked and recognised internationally. The other options (UNDP — development finance; UNESCO — education/culture; ITU — telecommunications) do not maintain occupational classification standards.
